body: AFAIK test instances are not CDI beans and so interceptors are not supported. However, we could make it work using `BeanManager.resolveInterceptors()`... we already use this kind of trick for MP rest client.

It might be easier to just make the test a bean, but it will result in fairly different behaviours between the native image and JVM mode ones. The behaviour is already different though so I don't know if that is really a problem.

> It might be easier to just make the test a bean...

I think we discussed this already and for some reason (I don't remember the details) we decided not to make them beans...

The conversation just kinda stalled, it was not really decided against. The original PR that made them beans had some unrelelated problems, and there was a lot of debate about how transactions should be handled, so it just kinda got lost.

I know we had to add quite some hacks because of the test instances are not beans - `InjectionPoint` metadata injection, skip removal of injected beans, etc. So if we decide to go this way (test instance -> bean instance) we should not forget to do a proper cleanup.

body: This wouldn't work even if the test instances were intercepted beans. "self-invocation" is not a business method from the CDI POV and so interceptors are not applied. Also why the private stuff?
A `doInTransaction` is a very useful thing. Where would it live?

QuarkusTransaction.doTransaction in the TX module would be my preference. There probably should be a method for each type of transaction attribute though, doInTransaction is not really clear if it would stay within an outer transaction or always create a new one.

Something like:

- `QuarkusTransaction.doInTransaction(Runnable)`
- `QuarkusTransaction.doInNewTransaction(Runnable)`
- `QuarkusTransaction.requiresTransaction(Runnable)`
- `QuarkusTransaction.doWithoutTransaction(Runnable)`
- `QuarkusTransaction.rejectTransaction(Runnable)`

If you can guess what the methods do, they are good names. If not they're as bad as the original enum, which is pretty terrible.

+1 for a `doInTransaction` helper. We have such helpers within the ORM testsuited and they've proven to be useful.

But let's start simple and not overload it too much? For example I wouldn't personally be able to guess what the differences are between `doInTransaction` and `doInNewTransaction`

Should we really use the _QuarkusX_ prefix ? Seems unnecessary to me.

My proposal would be to have `doInTransaction(Runnable)` doing the nested approach.
Then have an overloaded methid `doInTransaction(Transactional.TxType,Runnable)` to override the semantic the same way `@Transactional` would.
